Difficulty: Intermediate
THE CORE IDEA

For a competitive firm, short-run supply follows marginal cost (MC) at or above minimum average variable cost (AVC). Below minimum AVC, shutdown minimizes loss. Higher variable input costs shift MC and supply; higher fixed cost alone does not shift the short-run supply curve.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
Use the rising portion of marginal cost at and above minimum average variable cost as firm supply.
A variable-input cost increase shifts marginal cost and short-run supply upward or left.
A fixed-cost change shifts average total cost but leaves marginal cost and short-run supply unchanged.
Distinguish a movement along supply caused by price from a shift caused by production conditions.
WATCH OUT

Do not assume fixed cost shifts supply. The short-run supply schedule depends on marginal and variable costs, not fixed cost. Fixed cost affects profit but not the short-run MC-above-AVC supply schedule.
WORKED EXAMPLE: READING SHORT-RUN FIRM SUPPLY

The firm's short-run supply curve is the portion of MC at and above minimum AVC, which begins at point A: 22 units and $20. For example, if market price rises to $30, the firm supplies the quantity at point B, about 36 units. MC below A is not part of supply because the firm shuts down.
